free_tier.stated: MIT for Gitea and GPL for Forgejo, with a GitHub-Actions-compatible workflow syntax; unlimited on your own runners

per_object_cap.stated: no cap from the software; the runner host is the ceiling

interface_detail: a .forgejo/workflows or .gitea/workflows YAML; the act runner; a compatible subset of GitHub Actions
tooling: the forgejo or act runner binary; docker or a host backend
chaining: Actions syntax without GitHub, which lets a workflow move between a free hosted runner and your own machine without a rewrite

limits.value: no cap from the software; a documented subset of GitHub Actions is supported and the rest fails at parse time

reliability_note: compatibility with GitHub Actions is a documented subset, so a workflow that runs on GitHub may need edits
confidence_note: the Forgejo Actions user guide was read; Codeberg's hosted instance runs the same software.

evidence.proved: Forgejo Actions is GitHub-Actions-compatible with documented differences; runners are user-provided
Codeberg's hosted runners use ghcr.io/catthehacker/ubuntu:act-latest to provide a compatibility level with GitHub Actions, and Docker-in-Docker is not officially supported

notes: The compatibility is the value and the subset is the cost. A workflow that depends on a GitHub-only action does not run.
